sourceRefs.locator: Printed p. 627, entry beginning Her kyð on þissere bec. Old English text and translation: Ongynethel and Gythiccael, half a pound, four pence, two officials, church door and altar, named witnesses.

Scope and Content, post-Gospel additions: 51 records of manumission in Latin and Old English, marginal and blank-leaf entries. The catalogue’s broad dating should be read with Pracy’s discussion of individual hands and names.
The Haskins Society Journal 31, pp. 1 and 9, especially notes 40–43. Competing datings for entries sharing the name Maccos, around 1000 or late in the eleventh century.
National Heritage List for England 1355166, Location and Details, grid SX 07313 67033. The standing church is later than the entry and is used to locate Bodmin only.
